title: Kratom's 6,500% Problem
hook: Sold over the counter as a natural herb, kratom drove 19 U.S. poison center cases in 2010 and more than 1,200 in 2023 — with the severe outcomes climbing too.
key_points: U.S. poison center cases involving kratom rose from 19 in 2010 to more than 1,200 in 2023 — about a 6,500% increase.
Severe outcomes rose alongside the case count: life-threatening complications, lasting disability, and death.
Reported harms include seizures, abnormal heart rhythms, liver damage, and breathing problems.
Risk appears to increase when kratom is combined with other drugs.
Legal and 'natural' don't mean low-risk — kratom isn't regulated like a medicine.
content_html: Kratom is sold openly in the U.S. as a natural herbal supplement, often for pain or for easing off opioids. According to ScienceDaily's report on new research, U.S. poison center cases involving it went from 19 in 2010 to more than 1,200 in 2023 — and the share ending in life-threatening complications, lasting disability, or death climbed sharply as well.
extra_html:
The harms researchers describe aren't vague malaise: seizures, abnormal heart rhythms, liver damage, and trouble breathing. Risk looks higher when kratom is taken alongside other drugs, which is a common pattern given why people reach for it in the first place.

The broader lesson generalizes past kratom. Because it's sold as a supplement rather than a medicine, nobody has established a safe dose, mapped its drug interactions, or put warnings on the label. "Available at the gas station" carries no information about safety — and a steep rise in poison center calls is often the first place that shows up.

related.title: Understanding Addiction
related.hook: Addiction isn't a lack of willpower or a moral failing — it's a treatable medical condition that changes how the brain works. And like other chronic illnesses, it responds to treatment.

related.title: Using Pain Relievers Safely
related.hook: The pain relievers in your medicine cabinet are safe used right — and surprisingly risky used wrong. Knowing the two main types and their limits is the whole game.

related.title: A $70 Billion Industry With Thin Evidence
related.hook: Supplements are one of the fastest-growing corners of health spending. For most of what's on the shelf, there's little evidence it does what the label implies.

flashcards.back_html: It isn't regulated like a medicine — no vetted dose, no interaction labeling — while the poison center data shows real, rising harm.
